decisions.evidence: Read the authored definition against its suppliers. SH is stated in the library's strong line convention (def-suslin-line-order-interface: dense, no endpoints, Dedekind complete, ccc, nonseparable). Atomlessness is quantified over nonzero elements; ccc is correctly identified with B^+ = B minus zero under the stronger-is-smaller order of def-poset-ccc-and-knaster-property; the displayed diagonal law is the exact countable distributivity equation with both index sets omega; 0 != 1 excludes the one-element algebra and empty-bound conventions are fixed. No selection is made by the definition and the declared ZFC/AC boundary is honest.

Checked step by step against the complete source argument (Monk, Set theory following Jech, Lemma 9.12, printed pp. 65-68, retrieved and read in full from https://euclid.colorado.edu/~monkd/jech.pdf). Step 1.1 reproduces T1 = {t : T-up-t uncountable} and the countable-union/cone argument; 2.1 reproduces the branching-point cofinality argument and the least-branching-point construction making T** splitting, with the immediate-successor claim justified via T** contained in T*; 3.1 reproduces Monk's history-node order and its transitivity/tree verification; 4.1 reproduces the chain/antichain lifting; 4.2 reproduces the Hausdorff limit-level repair. Step 5.1's added claims are sound: between two consecutive limit levels there are infinitely many levels with at least 2^n nodes above any given node (distinct same-level nodes have distinct extensions at any higher level, since common extensions force comparability), so each retained node has countably infinitely many immediate successors in the retained tree, and the limit-level Hausdorff property follows by a least-difference argument using the next retained level below any node. The final cone has height omega_1 because an uncountable subtree of an omega_1-height tree cannot be confined to the countably many countable levels below any countable ordinal. AC uses are declared exactly where simultaneous choices occur.

Verified each step. The local successor orders exist because the refinement's successor sets are countably infinite (step 1.1 with thm-rationals-countable); maximal branches have countable limit length because a length-omega_1 branch would contradict Suslin and normality forbids a last node; the first-difference coordinate is a successor level (normal trees are Hausdorff at limit levels, so two branches agreeing at every lower level cannot split at a limit level), so the lex comparison is well defined. Step 4.1 reproduces Monk's Theorem 9.13 ccc argument (choose d(B,E),d(E,C) < alpha < len(E), map to level-alpha nodes; comparability forces E_eta inside I_xi, contradiction), which I checked against the retrieved source. Step 5.1's interval-nonseparability argument is correct: branches strictly between two branches that agree through level delta must pass through the level-delta node x (the first difference with each endpoint is at the same coordinate, so the branch lies on one side of both), hence have length > delta and escape the countable set D chosen below delta. Statement's imperative to order successor sets densely is realized by transport of the rational order and is consistent with the countably infinite successor sets.

Checked the cut construction and every claimed clause. Downward-closed cuts with all existing L-suprema included form a linearly ordered class (2.1 argument direction is correct), arbitrarily large families have suprema via U = union-X with the one-point closure U+{a} = (-inf,a] when a = sup_L U exists (the least-cut and infimum discussion is sound), and j(a) = (-inf,a] is an order embedding satisfying C1-C4 with the literal-inclusion convention. The uniqueness argument (tau_P(x) = {a in L : a <=_P x} is a cut, distinguishing elements uses C3 as x < y implies some a in L with x < a <= y, and sup_P X has trace X) is correct, as is the order-density transfer 5.2 including the x not in L case. The interval-ccc and interval-nonseparability transfers (6.1, 6.2) are checked in detail; deleting first/last elements preserves density, no-endpoints, bounded completeness and both transferred properties under the cumulative hypotheses (L dense plus the two interval conditions).

Composition checked clause by clause against def-suslin-line-order-interface. Step 1.1 instantiates the refinement supplier; 2.1 records dense/no-endpoint/interval-ccc/interval-nonseparability from the branch-order lemma; 3.1 applies the completion lemma (dense in, verify) and derives the final clause 'no countable order-dense subset' correctly: a countable order-dense set would meet every subinterval, making each nonempty open interval separable, which step 2.1's transferred property forbids. Nonemptiness, density, no endpoints, bounded completeness and interval ccc all come from the cited completions; the AC accounting matches the suppliers.

Defect phase-2-next-18-5a-c-001 (closed, fixed): step 5.1 inferred the nonemptiness of the endpointless quotient core from 'Q is not a singleton' alone, omitting the two-class case in which the deletion would leave nothing. Local repair added during this read: a two-class quotient would make S the union of two separable convex classes whose countable dense subsets meet every nonempty open interval of S (any interval is infinite and lies in I union J, so one part is infinite and contains a nonempty interval of that dense class), contradicting F1's nonseparability; hence Q has at least three classes. All other steps (1.1 convexity/transitivity of ~, 2.1 maximal disjoint families plus Zorn and the ccc bound, 3.1 density of the quotient, 4.1 four-case interval-nonseparability, 4.2 ccc lift, 5.1 completion) were checked against Monk Theorem 9.17 and the retrieved proof text. Contract boundaries 'one' and derivation d6 were updated; precheck passes.

Checked against Monk Theorem 9.18 and its proof (printed pp. 74-75, retrieved). Step 1.1's recursion is legitimate: the earlier endpoints form a countable set by thm-countable-union-of-countable, and because no nonempty interval of L is separable that set cannot be dense, so a nonempty interval misses it; density of L then places a_alpha < b_alpha inside. Step 2.1's dichotomy is exactly Monk's (1), predecessors are linearly ordered and well ordered, so (omega_1, prec) is a tree. 3.1 and 3.2 recover Monk's two ccc contradictions (successive nesting intervals; incomparable nodes give disjoint intervals). Step 4.1's height/countable-level argument is sound: levels are antichains hence countable, a countable height would make the carrier a countable union of countable levels, and no branch is cofinal (countable branch has countable supremum; uncountable chain excluded). Statement matches the supplier use in thm-suslin-line-implies-suslin-tree.

Two-step composition of the quotient lemma (F1, now repaired and rechecked) and the nested-interval tree lemma (F2). The hypotheses of F2 (dense, ccc, no endpoints, no separable nonempty interval) are exactly what F1 supplies, and the conclusion (height omega_1, countable levels, no cofinal branch, no uncountable antichain) is exactly the Suslin-tree definition of def-aronszajn-suslin-and-special-tree. No hidden hypothesis and no choice beyond the declared AC.

Verified against def-kappa-closure-distributivity-and-chain-condition and the standard argument. Step 1.1 correctly identifies forcing compatibility with tree comparability via the reverse order (both directions checked). Step 2.1 builds a maximal antichain A_D inside a dense open D using Zorn on antichains contained in D, notes maximality as a forcing antichain, bounds its heights (ccc plus countable-subset-of-omega_1 bound) and proves every node above that bound lies in D using comparability plus openness. Step 3.1 combines countably many dense opens with a single bound and normality's extension property to get density of the intersection, which is exactly aleph_1-distributivity. Step 4.1 applies the cited no-short-sequences supplier to the separative quotient (correctly, since the raw tree order is not separative when a node has one immediate successor) and preserves ordinals via the cited forcing theorem. Dependencies all exist and state what is used.

Checked every step. 1.1 nontriviality uses distinct bounds of a nonempty space; 2.1 atomlessness correctly splits below any chosen e(t) with two incompatible immediate successors and uses compatibility reflection so the two images are disjoint nonzero below b; 2.2 ccc injects a disjoint Boolean family into a forcing antichain (distinctness and incompatibility both argued); 2.3 the diagonal law argument is the standard density argument: r <= c is immediate, assuming 0 < d = c and not r one builds the dense-open sets D_n, uses the distributive identity a meet sup X = sup (a meet x) inside the density proof, appeals to aleph_1-distributivity for a common q <= p_0, and derives the contradiction e(q) <= r and e(q) <= not r. The identities used are proved or cited from the regular-open completion suppliers.

Checked the construction against the cited Jech 30.19/Bukovsky pattern. 1.1: the fixed selector s(a) gives a^0, a^1 nonzero disjoint with join a, including a = 1. 2.1/3.1: the recursion is well determined; at a limit lambda the countable union of earlier levels is countable (F5), the cofinal-sequence diagonalisation uses the exact countable distributivity law with each row joining to 1, and the argument that positive diagonal meets are coherent branch meets and that the level is an antichain with join 1 is correct (distinct branches differ at an earlier antichain level, giving disjoint meets). 4.1: each node has exactly one predecessor at each lower level, so the tagged union is a tree of height omega_1. 5.1: the extension property uses a meet/join distributivity computation to rule out a = 0, limit uniqueness follows from the branch-meet definition, and successor nodes have exactly the two immediate successors a^0, a^1. 5.2 and 6.1 give countable levels and no cofinal branch via the standard disjoint-difference antichain.

Three-way equivalence assembled from existing suppliers with no gap: ST=>SL from the tree-to-line theorem, SL=>ST from the line-to-tree theorem, ST=>SA by refining a Suslin tree to a normal splitting one and taking the regular-open completion, SA=>ST by the refining-antichain-tree construction. Negation then gives SH equivalent to the two nonexistence statements, matching SH as defined in def-suslin-hypothesis-and-suslin-algebra. The proof explicitly does not use the Recorded Kurepa remark.

Immediate from the refinement lemma and thm-splitting-suslin-tree-poset-square-not-ccc, whose statement I re-read: for a normal splitting Suslin tree the reverse-order poset is ccc while its coordinatewise square has the injective successor-pair antichain, hence is not ccc. The corollary's use of the refinement is legitimate because the refinement is normal and splitting and retains the Suslin prohibitions.

Standard specializing-forcing proof, checked against Karagila Proposition 7.4. Step 1.1: levels are nonempty, level injections plus a level representative give |T| = aleph_1 via omega_1 x omega absorption and Schroeder-Bernstein (both directions supplied). Step 2.1: P(T) is nonempty and ccc for an Aronszajn tree, and the family {D_t : t in T} has size aleph_1 so MA(aleph_1) supplies a filter meeting all of them; the directedness orientation matches lem-specialization-dense-domains-and-union. Step 3.1: the union is a total specializing map, fibers are antichains hence countable in a Suslin tree, and their countable union would make T countable, contradicting |T| = aleph_1. All cited suppliers exist and state exactly these facts.

Checked the cardinal bookkeeping: not-CH supplies a strictly intermediate set A for N and P(N); well-orderability converts the injections into aleph_0 < |A| < 2^{aleph_0} with strictness justified on both sides; |A| is a cardinal and aleph_1 is the least cardinal above aleph_0, so aleph_1 <= |A| < 2^{aleph_0}; the MA scheme therefore instantiates at aleph_1; the MA(aleph_1) theorem kills Suslin trees and the Kurepa equivalence turns that into SH. The MA definition's strict inequality is respected.

Definition read clause by clause: carrier is a countable subtree of the fixed sequence space with successor height, nonempty levels, restriction closure (giving the empty root), extension to every level at most alpha_p, and omega-splitting strictly below the top level; the top-level convention is explained and the order q <= p is literal end-extension, which is reflexive, transitive and antisymmetric. Clauses 2-4 do give normality in the sense of def-normal-splitting-set-theoretic-tree and clause 5 gives the infinitely-splitting strengthening used downstream. The choice ledger correctly states that forming the poset uses no choice and defers the later selections to the theorem.

Checked against Karagila Theorem 4.25 and Monk 15.31-15.38. 1.1: the lower bound for a descending eta-sequence uses delta = sup(alpha+1) < omega_1, the countable union U, the successor case (value attained, later conditions equal), and the limit case, where U is a countable normal omega-splitting tree of limit height and the sealing lemma supplies a countable top level of branch unions so that q = (delta, sealed U) is a condition end-extending every p_xi. 2.1 countable closure. 3.1: cf(omega_1)=omega_1 plus aleph_1-closure gives preservation; density of D_beta by iterated one-level extensions with closure at limit stages. 4.1: generic union T_G has levels at all beta, countable levels, normality and omega-splitting (successor levels literal, limit uniqueness by extensionality). 5.1-7.1: the fusion that decides a maximal antichain A* into a name and seals it at a higher top is the standard argument; each node of U is processed at the next outer stage, so A* is a countable maximal antichain of U, and q forces every future maximal antichain equal to A*. 8.1: ZFC in the extension, Zorn extends antichains, and a cofinal branch would give an uncountable antichain by the splitting-branch supplier.

Checked the finite-stage recursion in ZF. Step 1.2: B_n, C_n finite with max/min, strict preservation gives b < c when both exist, the gap I_n is nonempty in all four cases, and I_n avoids f_n[L_n] because every old point lies strictly on one side of x. Step 2.1: the least-index rule makes the transition single-valued, repetitions of e are handled by the e(n) in L_n branch, and induction preserves strictness. Step 3.1: coherence, domain L, order preservation and injectivity all follow from surjectivity of e plus well-ordering. The only witnesses used are the fixed e and rho, so no choice is used. Empty and finite orders are covered.

Checked both directions. 1.1 is immediate from the definition's equivalence. 1.2-1.3: the color function c(t) = least n with t in A_n, the finite-support binary codes g_t, and the least-differing-coordinate lexicographic order give an at most countable linear order G by a specified enumeration of finite binary words (no choice). 2.1: for s <_T t with colors m,n, disjointness of fibers gives m != n; the key coordinate bound g_s(n) = 0 < 1 = g_t(n) is proved in both cases n>m and n<m using the antichain property of the fiber of t; the first difference p satisfies p <= n and cannot have g_s(p)=1, g_t(p)=0 because a predecessor of s of color p <= c(t) would force g_t(p)=1. 3.1: the countable-order embedding supplier then gives q on T strictly increasing along the tree order. ZF throughout, and the remark correctly notes injectivity of t -> g_t is not needed.

Checked the internal forcing argument. 1.1 ccc and preservation from the Aronszajn hypothesis. 1.2 the canonical union name has value union-G and is a total specializing map by directedness (functionality and separation both justified by common extensions). 2.1 in the extension the tree keeps height omega_1 and has no cofinal branch: f restricted to a branch is injective into omega, so a cofinal branch would give an at most countable cofinal set of heights, contradicting the boundedness supplier. 3.1 fibers are antichains covering T; if all were countable T would be countable, again giving a countable cofinal height set. 4.1 the dense local arguments are converted to the internal forcing relation without asserting a universe generic.

Checked against Karagila 7.10-7.13. 1.1: ccc iteration preserves cardinals and cf(omega_2)=omega_2. 1.2: any Suslin tree in the extension has a canonical code C of size at most aleph_1 on omega_1. 2.1: the capture lemma puts C and the isomorphic presentation at a bounded stage, and Suslinity there is proved correctly by the persistence argument (an earlier uncountable level or antichain gives an injection from the preserved omega_1 which, composed with countability in the final model, would collapse omega_1; a cofinal branch persists). 3.1: the specialization forcing is coded and revisited cofinally with an isomorphic top-adjoined presentation on the branch met by G. 4.1: the successor quotient is forcing-equivalent to P(T*) by the dense embedding below the new top, so a total specialization exists and persists. 5.1: fibers are countable antichains whose countable union is omega_1, contradiction. The statement's scope (every supplied generic; internal reformulation only with externally available generics) is honest.

The splicing argument is a correct finite proof transformation: replace each SH-axiom line of a hypothetical certified ZFC+SH refutation by a variable-renamed copy of the fixed ZFC+MA+not-CH derivation of SH, redirecting references; the result is a certified refutation of ZFC+MA+not-CH, which is externally consistent by the cited supplier. The corollary is precise about its limits: it claims only an external implication, not a PA-verified uniform reduction, and does not extract a transitive model.

Checked the arithmetic reduction: the fixed ZF derivation that L satisfies ZFC and V=L, composed with the internal diamond?free route (V=L gives the normal splitting Suslin tree; tree-to-line inside L where AC holds) yields a fixed certified ZF proof of the literal L-relativization of not-SH. The dispatcher is extended by one decidable tag returning that constant proof block, primitive recursiveness and PA verification of checker acceptance are argued at the level of the existing verified translator, and the formal consistency implication then follows from the base-verified total reduction supplier. The corollary states exactly this and nothing more.

Both consistency claims come from the two formal-consistency corollaries under external Con(ZFC); the non-derivability steps are correct: a certified ZFC proof of SH becomes, in ZFC+not-SH, a refutation once the single added axiom and a fixed propositional contradiction block are appended, and symmetrically for a proof of not-SH. The theorem is explicit that it is conditional metamathematical independence, not an internal ZFC statement.

The eight terminal branches of 2^{<=3} and their lexicographic order 000<...<111 are correct, the adjacent-pair first-difference table checks out (for example 001<010 at coordinate 1 and 011<100 at coordinate 0), and the failure claims are witnessed explicitly: (000,010) = {001} is separable, 000 and 111 are endpoints, and ccc holds trivially. The example correctly isolates dense successor orders and unbounded splitting as the missing hypotheses, and uses no choice.

The three-stage configuration a_0 < a_2 < b_2 < a_1 < b_1 < b_0 is realized by the supplier's recursion: stage 1 inside the nonempty (a_0,b_0), stage 2 inside (a_0,a_1), which avoids the four earlier endpoints; the general trichotomy in 1.2 (inside, left, right, with boundary equality excluded because the new interval lies strictly inside the avoiding gap) is correct, as is the linear-ordering of predecessor sets in 4.1.

The refutation is correct and complete for the stated target. Branch 1: Con(ZFC) gives external Con(ZFC+MA+not-CH), and splicing the fixed derivation of SH from MA+not-CH into a hypothetical refutation of ZFC+SH+not-CH yields Con(ZFC+SH+not-CH), refuting SH=>CH. Branch 2: the L-interpretation dispatcher extended by constant blocks for the CH and not-SH tags gives PA-verified Con(ZFC)->Con(ZFC+CH+not-SH), refuting CH=>SH; the remark correctly notes that the joint consistency needs the combined dispatcher rather than separate marginal claims. Both branches keep the distinction between external and internal results.

The example mirrors the theorem's fusion accurately: the distinction between a ground antichain and a name (1.1), the two-dimensional fusion with inner decisions made persistent and counted into A* (2.1), coverage of every node of U by the next outer enumeration (3.1), and the sealing and future-node argument (4.1-5.1). The omega-union losing its top and the sealing restoring one is exactly what the definition requires.

Checked the explicit computations: the density extension q = p union {(t,N)} with N above every old label is a specializing condition and meets D_t (including the empty-condition and label-zero cases); directedness makes f a function, totality follows from meeting every D_t, and comparable nodes receive distinct labels; the fibers are antichains covering T, one of them uncountable by the countable-union/boundedness contradiction; the branch-injectivity argument shows Aronszajnness persists. The example correctly restricts itself to a supplied generic and refers internal consequences to the theorem.

Definition read: successor stages are two-step iterations, limits are inverse limits of coherent functions with at most countable nontrivial support, order is coordinatewise with top-name coordinates treated as trivial, and the restriction/quotient convention is stated. The closing paragraph is honest that the countable-support union of coherent initial segments is a separate obligation rather than a hidden closure assumption, and that the definition makes no choice.

Definition read: (M,P)-genericity is D-intersect-M predense below q for every dense D in M, spelled out in the stronger-is-smaller convention; master below p; properness quantified over all sufficiently large regular theta and all p in P-intersect-M. The item explicitly says genericity does not require q in every dense set and that the club formulation is proved later, not assumed. No choice is used by the definition.

Checked the cycle (i)=>(ii)=>(iii)=>(iv)=>(i). The 1.1 equivalence is standard predensity-versus-forcing. 2.1: the reverse inclusion uses a maximal antichain for a name in M, predensity to find a compatible decider, and elementarity to place the decided value in M. 3.1: mixing a name for the index of the generic antichain member, then (iv) applies to that ordinal name; the conclusion that A-intersect-M is predense below q is the correct reading of a member of A forced into the generic filter. 4.1: club formulation equivalence by absorbing a subclub as the models closed under a function, with the least well-order witness; D-intersect-N = D-intersect-M since D is a subset of H_mu.

Both halves checked. Ccc: a maximal antichain A inside a dense D is countable by ccc and, being a countable element of the elementary model, is a subset of it (the countability of A in the universe transfers to M by elementarity of the satisfaction of 'A is countable' with parameter A in M, whose witness surjection then has range inside M); hence A is contained in D-intersect-M and p itself is a master. Countably closed: enumerate the dense sets in M, choose p_{n+1} in D_n-intersect-M below p_n by elementarity, apply countable closure; the lower bound is a master. The empty-antichain exceptional case cannot occur because a maximal antichain of a nonempty poset is nonempty.

Checked the standard master-model argument. 1.1: an elementary model whose trace delta lies in the stationary set exists by the club/stationarity argument; delta is a countable limit ordinal. 2.1: the continuous increasing enumeration name of the club is in M, each index alpha<delta is in M, the master forces those values into M-intersect-omega_1 = delta, so the first delta values are cofinal in delta and closure of the club gives delta in the club; the ground ordinal delta lies in S, giving the required intersection. 3.1: preservation of omega_1 is proved by the same master argument on functions from omega rather than by a hidden cofinality inference.

Checked against Jech's proper iteration lemma. Successor case (2.1): the induction hypothesis places the earlier master, properness of the last iterand in the intermediate extension supplies an (M[G_beta],Q_beta)-master, and the two-step genericity is transferred to (M,P_{beta+1})-genericity by the ordinal-name argument. Limit case (2.2-3.1): the fusion through a cofinal sequence gamma_n from M-intersect-alpha works because each recursive step projects a dense set and applies the induction hypothesis at gamma_{n+1}<alpha; the union over coherent initial segments has countable support and is a condition, with no coordinatewise lower bound in an arbitrary proper iterand; the limit conclusion uses that a name in M has support inside M-intersect-alpha, bounded by rho. 4.1: each D_n-intersect-M is predense below q, so q is a master, and its restriction to gamma_0 is q_0.

Immediate application of the master lemma at gamma=0 with the trivial stage P_0, whose unique condition is generic and forces the ground name p into P_alpha-intersect-M. The statement correctly restricts the hypotheses to iterands forced proper by their preceding stage and asserts no closure of the iterands.

Definition read: PFA is stated for nonempty proper partial orders and families of at most omega_1 dense sets, with the stronger-is-smaller filter convention, explicit inclusion of empty and finite families, and an explicit note that the bound is fixed at omega_1 rather than FA_{<2^{aleph_0}}(proper). No value of the continuum is presupposed and the definition makes no selection.

PFA is applied to ccc posets, which are proper by the ccc-implies-proper theorem, giving MA(aleph_1); the MA(aleph_1) theorem kills Suslin trees; the Kurepa equivalence converts this to SH. Each step uses the exact hypotheses of its supplier and no value of the continuum.

Definitions read against Todorcevic's usage: modulo-finite containment, orthogonality, ideals of countable subsets, P-ideals, PID's two alternatives, strong finite intersection property, pseudointersection, the pseudointersection number p, and S-spaces as regular Hausdorff hereditarily separable non-Lindelof spaces. The conventions (finite sets included, empty-intersection clause for SFIP, regular plus Hausdorff both required) are explicit and the choice cost of the cardinal p is declared.

Re-read: the forcing is sigma-centered, the dense sets E_a and D_n are as claimed, and the filter argument yields an infinite pseudointersection for every at most omega_1 SFIP family, so p > omega_1. No step depends on an unstated hypothesis.

The proof is a faithful compression of Moore's published argument (retrieved and read in full: Moore-Venturi, sections 3.2 and 4-5). Step 1.1 defines the poset Q_I with the finite Z, the membership chain, the separation clause and the side condition X-intersect-Z contained in N; step 2.1 reproduces Moore's Lemma 4.3 properness verification: thickening the side chain by M-intersect-H_theta, the r_0/n thinning of D, the J-plus-splitting T' via the sigma-ideal J generated by I-perp (with the otherwise-first-deletion contradiction using the side condition at the added model), the successive choices of initial segments by elementarity, the infinite H in I meeting all relevant I_P, and the resulting common extension. Step 3.1 reproduces the density argument: the uncountability of the generic Z via the master condition and x outside every M-intersect-I-perp, the ground-model countable covering by side models, and the conclusion that every countable subset of Z lies in I. Step 4.1 reproduces the final omega_1-density argument with PFA and the coherent decided values. Each claim of the compressed text corresponds to a step of the source proof I checked.

Checked against Todorcevic's Section 23 argument (retrieved). 1.1: a non-Lindelof subspace yields x_alpha and neighborhoods U_alpha with U_alpha-intersect-X countable by the recursion through omega_1, and closed V_x with V_x-bar inside U_x; the ideal I of countable sets meeting each closed neighborhood finitely is an ideal. 2.1: the domination fact is proved from the definition of p through the sets A_f and C_n and thinning a pseudointersection to a dominator g; applied to the row functions f_x with |X| = omega_1 < p it gives a pseudounion in I, so I is a P-ideal. 3.1: the first PID alternative yields an uncountable discrete (hence non-separable) subspace. 3.2: in the second alternative the family D minus closed neighborhood has the strong finite intersection property (otherwise Y is covered by finitely many countable U_x-intersect-X) and a pseudointersection a lies in I while being contained in Y, contradicting orthogonality. Both alternatives contradict hereditary separability.

Defect phase-2-next-18-5a-c-003 (closed, fixed): step 1.1 wrote '$mathfrak p>omega_1$' without the backslashes used in the same file's F2 and F3 lines; the display was repaired to '$\\mathfrak p>\\omega_1$', with no change to the claim. The corollary itself is the immediate combination of PFA implies PID, PFA implies p > omega_1, and PID plus p > omega_1 eliminates S-spaces.

The comparison is accurate: Laver preparation makes kappa indestructible under a restricted class of directed-closed forcings, while the PFA iteration uses the Laver function to guess arbitrary proper names and deliberately collapses cardinals so that kappa becomes omega_2. The remark correctly states that the preparation theorem is comparison material and not a premise, and asserts no proper-preservation of supercompactness.

Definition read against Cummings's Theorem 24.11 construction: countable-support iteration of length kappa where stage alpha uses the Laver guess when it is a P_alpha-name forced to be a nonempty proper order with a greatest condition, and the one-condition fallback otherwise; the internal nature of the test is explained, and the collapse factors and the stage-kappa identification of an anticipated name are stated as consequences of the definition plus the next lemma, not as extra clauses.

Checked against Cummings, Proposition 7.13 and Theorem 24.11 (retrieved and read). 1.1 properness by the iteration theorem. 2.1: hereditary size below kappa by induction using inaccessibility and bounded countable supports at uncountable-cofinality limits; the Delta-system thinning with a bounded root, regularity thinning on root restrictions, and the union argument give kappa-Knaster and hence kappa-cc with |P_kappa| at most kappa. 3.1: the Laver reflection argument supplies the collapse Col(omega_1,alpha) cofinally often, collapsing every ground cardinal between omega_1 and kappa and giving |P_kappa| at least kappa; kappa stays a cardinal by kappa-cc, so kappa = omega_2 in the extension. 4.1: for an embedding anticipating a forced-proper name, elementarity makes the first kappa stages equal P_kappa, closure preserves the properness assertion, and the tail factors as stated; this is the source's factorization step.

Checked against Cummings Theorem 24.11's semantic argument. 1.1-2.1: the name normalization Q-star (restrict below p and adjoin a greatest condition, with the one-condition value on the incompatible side) is forced by every condition to be nonempty, proper and to have a greatest condition, and the given dense sets remain dense in Q-star; the empty-family case is handled separately. 3.1-4.1: the anticipated embedding, the factorization j(P_kappa) = P_kappa * Q-star * R, the common outer universe generics g and H, and the lifted elementary embedding j_G defined on name values (well-defined by the forcing theorem and bounded supports) follow the source. 5.1: the image-generated filter on j_G(Q-star) meets every image dense set, and elementarity reflects the existence of a filter meeting all D_xi back to V[G], where intersecting with Q and using directedness below the adjoined top produces a genuine filter on Q. 6.1: arbitrary generic gives the forced statement.

Compiler structure checked against its declared suppliers (lem-forcing-transfer-for-finite-zfc-fragments, thm-formal-consistency-transfer-by-forcing): the formula-code forcing recursion, the axiom constructor with the single PFA tag and the schematic branches, the finite fragment output with exactly the used source axioms, the bounded primitive-recursive operations, and the PA induction over decoded lines producing the required verified total reduction. The item matches the supplier requirement that semantic correctness alone is insufficient and that support extraction and constructors must be verified.
